symbolic_guard: shared inherited IO phase plus static ParamRTL port-shape validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited IO-shape guard on the concrete witness, while ParamRTL retains a static named port direction and packed-type schema for every legal parameter value.

symbolic_guard: shared inherited hierarchy phase plus ParamRTL module dependency, mixed-local dependency, generate-scope and typed named-binding validation
rationale: MorphVerilog runs the inherited hierarchy phase on the concrete witness; ParamRTL separately validates the symbolic module graph, typed bindings, one combined local graph, bounded generate-for scope, both generate-if branches and every generate-case choice/default, while default-shape recursion substitutes bindings and recomputes mixed locals per instance.

symbolic_guard: ParamRTL symbolic expression, portable address-width, mixed local-parameter, Boolean-expression, integer-comparison, conditional-integer, indexed-part-select, runtime-process and bounded-memory type/capacity proof
rationale: The concrete witness runs the shared inherited phase and the guarded frontend preserves implemented constant expressions, portable address-width expressions and direct runtime-process/memory port references for ParamRTL proof. Bound public defaults are evaluated per instance before the combined dependency-first local graph, conditional child locals and widths are recomputed. ParamRTL proves AddressWidth has a positive operand domain, returns at least one, preserves exact power-of-two boundaries and correlates a memory address port with that memory's depth; target capability separately enforces the signed-32-bit ceiling. Combinational conditions and sequential clock/reset/enable controls are exact unsigned one-bit inputs, while runtime and memory data paths are exactly type-compatible with their targets for the complete legal width domain. Conditional intervals conservatively hull both branches without guard correlation; general runtime expressions and general-purpose minimum, maximum and clog2 remain planned.

symbolic_guard: predicate-aware ParamRTL driver and bounded process/memory coverage
rationale: The concrete witness runs the inherited phase and ParamRTL proves exact output coverage for canonical generate-for, generate-if and generate-case configurations, both paths of one complete CombinationalIf, sole ownership by each atomic register variant and sole read-output/memory ownership for the bounded memory. Each enabled register's absent disabled assignment is intentional sequential hold; the memory's unwritten content is explicit unspecified state, not an incomplete combinational driver. Mixed procedural/structural drivers fail before emission; general expressions, multiple or nested runtime statements and broader sequential/memory forms keep the guard partial.

symbolic_guard: atomic ParamRTL register and synchronous-memory completeness/ownership proof
rationale: Increments 16 through 19 admit atomic rising-edge registers only when the sole output has a complete reset/capture/hold policy. Increment 20 adds one atomic synchronous memory whose read output is assigned on every edge, whose optional write is intentional storage retention and whose surplus address has a complete zero/no-write policy. No sibling process, hierarchy, generate or continuous driver is allowed. General clocked statements, arbitrary hold values, multiple registers and broader memory/process coverage remain unimplemented, so the disposition stays partial.

symbolic_guard: shared graph check plus symbolic generate analysis
rationale: The Increment 15 direct input-to-output combinational process and Increment 16 through 19 direct input-to-register-output processes cannot encode a combinational feedback edge, while the inherited concrete graph guard still runs. Intentional enabled hold is state feedback, not a combinational path. General runtime expressions require a ParamRTL dependency-graph adaptation before this disposition can advance.

symbolic_guard: one-clock bounded process/memory restriction plus shared concrete CDC check
rationale: Increments 16 through 20 each encode one validated unsigned one-bit input clock and forbid sibling processes, hierarchy and generate structure, so an internal multi-domain crossing is unrepresentable in each tranche. They do not model or approve external input-domain provenance, multiple clocks or CDC structures, so the broader CDC disposition remains partial.
The shared finalizer rejects leaked DSL and clock-domain stacks after configured phase inserters; PhaseContext.doPhase independently keeps every pending phase error fatal.
